name: Today's Report
headline: Bay Area home prices kept pace with inflation while the nation's slipped for a 16th month.
teaser: Bay Area home prices kept pace with inflation while the national Case-Shiller index trailed it for a 16th month, mortgage rates fell to 7.26%, consumer confidence rose to 103.3, China kept its minerals pause through January, and chip stocks slid again.

sections.label: Real estate
sections.html:
Home prices trailed inflation again. S&P's Case-Shiller national index rose 2.1% in the year to September while consumer prices rose 3.7%, the 16th straight month home prices fell after inflation, S&P said Tuesday. Market Briefs had those numbers right.

The Bay Area kept pace. The San Francisco metro index, which covers Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, San Francisco and San Mateo counties, rose 3.73%, fifth of 19 metros and even with inflation to the rounding. Only Chicago, New York, Miami and Cleveland beat inflation.

Rates fell. Mortgage News Daily's 30-year average is 7.26%, down 0.06 from Tuesday and 0.20 from a week ago, with the 15-year at 6.82%. On today's $1,218,320 Fremont median with 20% down, that is about $6,655 a month in principal and interest.

What it means for you. If you own here, your home has about held its value after inflation over the past year, which most of the country cannot say. If you are buying, the holiday weeks bring fewer competing buyers, and 191 homes in our five cities have been on the market 60 days or longer.

Today's count. Board wide: 2,157 listings across the 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, down from 2,207 Tuesday, with 139 coming soon and 66 brand new. The five city ledger carries 555 live listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City, 482 on the market and 73 coming soon, down from 562.

Fremont holds 196 live listings: 157 active, 28 coming soon and 9 brand new, with a median on market list price of $1,218,320 at $783 a square foot and a typical listing out 41 days. Hayward carries 156, Milpitas 82, Newark 67 and Union City 54. Across all five cities the median is $999,894 at $667 a square foot, 244 homes are priced under a million, and 191 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

images.alt: Ranked bar chart of S&P Cotality Case-Shiller home price changes in the year to September 2026 for 19 metros, against inflation of 3.74%: Chicago 6.9%, New York 5.8%, Miami 4.6%, Cleveland 4.0%, San Francisco metro 3.73% (highlighted), down to Seattle at minus 1.9%. U.S. national 2.1%.
images.caption: The San Francisco metro's 3.73% gain kept pace with inflation; only four metros beat it.

sections.label: Economy
sections.html:
Consumers are in a better mood. The Conference Board's consumer confidence index rose 11.4 points to 103.3 in November, back to levels last seen in January 2025, as 30.8% of consumers said jobs are plentiful, up from 26.2% in October. Plans to buy homes improved slightly, though consumers still expect 5.7% inflation over the next year.

China kept its minerals pause. China kept its ban on U.S.-bound gallium, germanium and antimony on hold through Jan. 27, Bloomberg reported Tuesday, extending a pause that was due to end Friday. The U.S. Geological Survey puts China's share of 2025 world production at 99% for low purity gallium, used in chips, 80% for natural graphite, used in batteries, and 36% for mined antimony, where Russia and Tajikistan together mine nearly half.

The 10-year Treasury closed at 4.85%, down 0.06 point. Gold settled at $3,535.80, down 0.73%, and silver at $40.06, down 1.78%. Brent settled Tuesday at $91.40, up 2.27%.

Shoppers are feeling better just in time for Black Friday. Their credit cards get the final say.

images.alt: Stacked bar chart of China's share of world production in 2025: low purity gallium 99%, natural graphite 80% (Madagascar 5% and Tanzania 4% next), mined antimony 36% (Russia 29% and Tajikistan 20% next).
images.caption: China produces 99% of the world's low purity gallium and 80% of its natural graphite.

sections.label: Stocks
sections.html:
Nvidia slid for a second day. It fell 3.91% to $149.30, leaving it 19.9% below where it started the year, and Micron lost 4.53%. The Nasdaq fell 0.62% and the S&P 500 0.25%, while the Dow rose 0.33% to 50,182.95. Anthropic rose 1.08% to $82.79, still below its $83 offering price.

A short week. Markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving, and Friday's session ends early, at 10 a.m. Pacific. Chip investors could use the long weekend.

sections.label: Crypto
sections.html:
Bitcoin edged back above $60,000. It was near $60,093 at 2:05 PM PT, up 0.32% over 24 hours on CoinGecko. Ether was near $1,682.53 (+0.09%) and XRP near $0.94 (+1.78%).

Crypto did not follow chips down today. After seven losing weeks, a quiet day counts as progress.
